text:
maria: Customer (ACME) reporting big latency spikes and intermittent 403s starting ~2026-09-12 11:02 UTC after heavy EU traffic. They say a bunch of requests were routed to us-east and auth started rejecting them. Link to customer logs: https://acme.s3/trace-req_0a1b2c3d (redacted).

chris: Can you paste a sample request/response and confirm Hosted vs Dedicated? Any client-side retries?

maria: Hosted. Sample curl I ran and the failure: ```curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "x-region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"token_audience_mismatch"}```

deepa: From metrics, eu-west reached ~98% of allocatable GPU capacity at 11:01 and our fallback policy kicked in. Fallback policy is 'fallback_to_secondary' (us-east). That explains cross-region routing, but 403 points to token audience mismatch when forwarded.

lee: We did a token-scope rollout last week that tightens audience to include region claim. If requests are forwarded to us-east with a eu-scoped token, auth rejects them. The canary didn't exercise forwarded paths.

maria: Repro steps I ran for validation:
1) hammer 20 parallel requests with x-region: eu-west-1
2) observe ~40-60% routed to us-east when queueing spikes
3) those routed requests return 403 token_audience_mismatch
Logs: ```[2026-09-12T11:01:05Z] req=req_0a1b2c3d routed=us-east auth_err=token_audience_mismatch```

infra-bot: System: RoutingPolicy 'fallback_to_secondary' activated for region=eu-west-1 at 2061234500, spill_count=7720, queue_depth=410.

chris: Assigning to @lee and @deepa to triage and confirm a mitigation. Also customer is flagging an unexpected billing jump from retries — can we check retry counting behavior?

deepa: Checked logs — many clients didn't set idempotency key; our client-side retry guidance says to include it. Retries that arrive as new requests were billed each time. We'll arrange a partial credit for the customer while we fix the root cause.

lee: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) push sticky-region override TTL=600s for this customer's org to prevent fallback for their traffic 2) scale up eu-west pool by +2 nodes (temporary). I can deploy the override in ~2m.

maria: Customer accepted the sticky pin and temporary credits. After applying pin+scale, I retried the same repro and saw 100% served from eu-west with p95 ~200ms and no 403s.

chris: For the permanent fix: update fallback auth handling so forwarded requests are either re-issued a compatible token or we allow region-scoped tokens when forwarding. Also raise spillover threshold from 0.92 -> 0.97 and add gradual shedding to avoid sudden cascades.

deepa: I'll own the postmortem. Preliminary root causes: (a) under-provisioned eu-west for that workload pattern, (b) aggressive spillover policy causing cross-region forwarding, (c) token-audience mismatch not covered by canary, (d) retry/billing edge-case for clients without idempotency. Action items: scale targets, adjust policy, add alarm for 'fallback_rate', add integration test that simulates token scope with forwarded paths, and ensure runbook includes billing-credit play.

maria: Noted customer contact and credit. I'll update the support ticket and mark as mitigated once postmortem link is up. Ticket: INC-2061 (auto).

support-bot: Ticket INC-2061 updated: status=investigating -> mitigated. Runbook: routing-fallback -> note added (token-scope caveat).
